checkpointShape: one Uint32 FNV state per file boundary
externalStateHashCompatibility: legacy canonical FNV hash preserved exactly
universalHashFallback: ordinary untracked hashValue(value) remains the sealed v0.17 adaptive policy
question: Can one trusted point mutation advance exact canonical-size metadata, the existing canonical FNV state fingerprint, the mutation receipt, and the existing versioned domain identity from the same event while preserving full recomputation as an oracle/fallback?

mechanism.bootstrap: Store the legacy-compatible FNV state immediately before each canonical file body.
mechanism.pointMutation: Reuse the unchanged prefix checkpoint, hash the changed file and canonical suffix, refresh downstream checkpoints, then advance canonical-size metadata and the existing v0.10 domain identity from the same mutation event.
mechanism.structuralFallback: File-count/top-level-envelope changes are rejected by the checkpoint point-mutation path rather than guessed compatible.

first.interpretation: Near-no-benefit structural counterexample: exact legacy FNV compatibility leaves almost the entire suffix after a first-file mutation.

sameWidthLast.interpretation: Canonical representation size stays exactly unchanged while state hash and the imports/content-hash domain identities advance.

proofBoundary.exactness: v0.19 and v0.20 end at the same legacy-compatible FNV state hash, exact canonical size, changed-domain receipt, and versioned domain identity in every measured scenario.
proofBoundary.oneEvent: v0.20 uses one trusted point-mutation event to advance canonical-size metadata, exact state fingerprint checkpoints, the mutation receipt, and the existing v0.10 domain identity.
proofBoundary.checkpointCost: The 2,500-file checkpoint body is a persistent 10,000-byte Uint32Array.
proofBoundary.positionBoundary: The implemented exact legacy-FNV checkpoint path reuses the unchanged prefix but still rehashes the changed file and canonical suffix. It is position-sensitive and is not claimed O(1).
proofBoundary.timing: Five fresh processes per method/scenario. Bootstrap/checkpoint construction and independent full-reference verification are excluded. Hosted timing medians are observations, not universal performance claims.
proofBoundary.compatibility: No new Merkle/state-hash identity is introduced. The external state hash remains byte-for-byte compatible with the existing canonical FNV fingerprint.
proofBoundary.scope: This is a deterministic 2,500-file workspace harness. It is not a datacenter, fleet, energy, or universal software claim.

strongestSupportedClaim: In this deterministic 2,500-file tracked-workspace harness, one trusted point mutation can advance exact canonical-size metadata, the existing legacy-compatible canonical FNV state hash, its mutation receipt, and the existing versioned domain identity from one event. A 10,000-byte file-boundary FNV checkpoint body enables exact unchanged-prefix reuse: a middle-file path mutation reduced canonical fingerprint rehashing from 1,284,860 to 650,693 characters and median measured transition time from 25.31 ms to 14.55 ms; a last-file path mutation reduced rehashing to 575 characters with the exact same state/domain truth and measured 4.41 ms versus 25.08 ms. A first-file mutation preserved the near-no-benefit counterexample, saving only 27 canonical characters. Timing is hosted evidence, not universal performance.
nextGate: v0.21 checkpointed domain truth advance: test whether changed domain-entry hashes can reuse exact prefix checkpoints too, while accounting for the persistent checkpoint tax and retaining first-file/two-domain counterexamples.
